season_storylines: Patrick Mahomes is rehabbing a torn ACL and LCL and pushing hard for Week 1, so his 6-pt-TD premium comes with real availability risk while Rashee Rice (knee cleanup) is still expected to start Week 1.

Bijan Robinson (ATL) and Jahmyr Gibbs (DET) are both holding in at camp over contract extensions; neither is practicing as of this weekend, and any deal or escalation directly moves two top-5 non-PPR RBs.

The QB carousel reshaped half the league: Tua Tagovailoa to Atlanta (now nursing a back flare-up with Michael Penix Jr. still not cleared off his ACL), Kyler Murray to Minnesota (verify starter status), Kirk Cousins to the Raiders, Geno Smith to the Jets, and Malik Willis starting in Miami.

Sean Payton's coaching tree took over the AFC: Declan Doyle installs a play-action-heavy offense in Baltimore that Lamar Jackson called mind-blowing, Joe Brady runs a slow run-heavy Bills offense, and Klint Kubiak brings under-center play-action to Las Vegas promising Ashton Jeanty a McCaffrey-style role.

Mike McDaniel landed as Chargers OC under Jim Harbaugh, importing the Achane-style catch-and-run scheme that boosts Omarion Hampton's yardage ceiling and Ladd McConkey's volume, though short catches are worth less in non-PPR.
A.J. Brown was moved to New England to pair with a healthy Drake Maye, giving the Patriots a 10.5 win total and giving Brown the downfield TD-heavy usage that plays up at zero-PPR.

Zach Charbonnet tore his ACL in Seattle, clearing the lane for Jadarian Price, while Kenneth Walker III signed with Kansas City where Eric Bieniemy's return signals an explosive-run emphasis behind Mahomes or his fill-in.

Malik Nabers' ACL-plus-meniscus recovery (with a spring scar-tissue cleanup) is genuinely uncertain for Week 1, dragging down the whole Giants pass game while Cam Skattebo is further along and expected to start at RB.

Betting markets stack Baltimore and the Rams at 11.5 wins as the top offenses to buy, while Arizona (3.5, lowest in the league despite No. 3 overall pick Jeremiyah Love), Miami (4.5) and the Raiders/Jets/Browns (5.5) profile as negative-script, low-team-total environments.

Season-long IDP/DST ripples from camp: Micah Parsons (now GB) is out until at least September and maybe the postseason with a torn ACL, Nic Scourton (CAR) and Bryan Bresee (NO) are done for the year, and Shemar Stewart (CIN) is in a leg brace awaiting imaging.

teams.outlook: New HC Mike LaFleur (Shanahan/McVay tree) inherits the league-low 3.5 win total but hands No. 3 overall pick Jeremiyah Love a three-down role with Tyler Allgeier complementing, so Love's TD equity is the only premium asset while James Conner is buried on the depth chart.

Kevin Stefanski's zone-run scheme should feed Bijan Robinson 20-plus weekly touches once his hold-in ends, but the QB room is a mess with Tua's back flare-up and Penix's ACL, capping the pass-game and keeping this a run-funnel offense.

New OC Declan Doyle's Payton-style play-action offense drew rave reviews from Lamar Jackson, the win total is a league-high 11.5, and Derrick Henry behind an upgraded line is a premium non-PPR TD hammer.

New HC Joe Brady keeps play-calling with a deliberately slow, run-heavy identity, which concentrates value in Josh Allen's rushing TDs and James Cook's carries while newcomer DJ Moore gets a QB upgrade but a modest target ceiling.

Dave Canales is giving Jonathon Brooks first-team reps over Chuba Hubbard after two ACL rehabs, rookie WR Chris Brazzell II is out about 8 weeks with an LCL tear, and a 7.5 win total suggests more competitive scripts than last year.

Ben Johnson retains play-calling for an offense that was 2nd in plays and 6th in yards, and DJ Moore's exit leaves roughly 150 vacated targets pointing at Luther Burden III, whose 2.92 yards per route run sits in Nacua/JSN territory.

The offense returns intact around Burrow-Chase-Higgins with a 10.5 win total, while the front office spent on defense (Dexter Lawrence, Jonathan Allen) to fix game scripts, which mildly trims garbage-time passing volume but stabilizes the whole offense's floor.

Todd Monken now runs the show with a Ravens-style ground game (verify HC structure), and with the QB room unsettled Quinshon Judkins, fully recovered from his fractured fibula, is the offense's centerpiece and a volume-based non-PPR RB2.
The Cowboys sit at a quiet 9.5 win total after spending on defense (Rashan Gary, Jalen Thompson), leaving the offensive pecking order stable, so the fantasy angle is continuity rather than change.

Sean Payton traded a first for Jaylen Waddle to be his catch-and-run alpha, but Bo Nix is coming off two ankle procedures (expected Week 1), so Waddle's YAC-driven yardage plays fine in non-PPR only if Nix's mobility is genuinely back.

New OC Drew Petzing brings elite explosive-run design to a 10.5-win roster, which is great for Jahmyr Gibbs once his contract hold-in resolves, with Isiah Pacheco added as insurance and the Kerby Joseph/Brian Branch injuries weakening the defense enough to add shootout risk.

Jordan Love's group is stable at a 9.5 win total, but Josh Jacobs is 28 with 2,109 career touches and a falling 4.0 YPC, and Micah Parsons' ACL (out until at least September, maybe the year) hurts the DST play.

Houston rebuilt the OL (Wyatt Teller, Braden Smith) and added David Montgomery to fix the run game, the exact conditions C.J. Stroud needs to rebound, with sophomore Jayden Higgins' TD-per-target profile a sneaky non-PPR add.

Daniel Jones says he is fully cleared from his torn Achilles and the offense returns its identity, but Alec Pierce may miss the whole preseason with his ankle, so early-season field-stretching falls to others and Jonathan Taylor remains the anchor.

Travis Etienne's exit leaves Bhayshul Tuten, who scored 7 TDs on just 93 touches with a 31% missed-tackle rate, as the TD-efficiency breakout, while Travis Hunter plans to play primarily cornerback, which torpedoes his WR fantasy value.

Eric Bieniemy is back as OC with an explosive-run emphasis and Kenneth Walker III imported to carry it, which insulates the offense while Mahomes pushes his ACL/LCL rehab toward Week 1; Rashee Rice is expected ready despite the knee cleanup.

New OC Mike McDaniel brings the quick-game, catch-and-run scheme to Herbert, McConkey and Omarion Hampton, and Hampton's dual-threat yardage plus goal-line work makes him the clearest non-PPR winner of the scheme change.

McVay continuity plus a Myles Garrett trade puts the Rams at a league-high 11.5 wins, keeping Nacua, Adams and Kyren Williams locked in, though 38-year-old Stafford is the single point of failure for the whole stack.

Klint Kubiak's under-center play-action offense with Kirk Cousins at QB is built around Ashton Jeanty being used like Christian McCaffrey and Brock Bowers as the passing-game centerpiece, but the 5.5 win total means negative scripts will test the run commitment.

New HC Jeff Hafley and OC Bobby Slowik inherit a teardown at a league-worst-tier 4.5 wins with Malik Willis at QB, so De'Von Achane (79.6% career zone runs, minor shoulder cleanup, ready Week 1) is the only core asset and volume is the argument, not efficiency.

Kyler Murray arrives (verify he holds the job all year) with Jauan Jennings added alongside Justin Jefferson, and Murray's rushing floor keeps him a viable 6-pt-TD QB even at a middling 8.5-win projection.
A.J. Brown joins a fully healthy Drake Maye (shoulder required no surgery) on a 10.5-win roster, and Brown's downfield TD-heavy profile is exactly the archetype that beats slot compilers in non-PPR.

Tyler Shough closed his rookie year with six straight 17-plus-point fantasy games and now gets Travis Etienne and rookie WR Jordyn Tyson (verify), making the Saints a sneaky volume offense despite a 7.5 win total, while Chris Olave's role is being squeezed.

A new regime with OC Matt Nagy (verify HC situation) leans run-heavy, drafting a fullback and installing Cam Skattebo, fully recovered from his tibia fracture, as the starting RB, while Jaxson Dart's development and Nabers' knee define the passing ceiling.
Robert Saleh is back as HC with Frank Reich calling a run-first offense for Geno Smith, which makes Breece Hall a volume-based non-PPR anchor on a bad 5.5-win team and caps every Jets pass catcher.

A new offensive staff (Kellen Moore HC per reports - verify) with first-time play-caller Sean Mannion shifts to under-center wide zone, and Saquon Barkley's yards-before-contact collapse from 2.64 to 1.36 makes his workload-heavy profile more fragile than his name suggests.

Mike McCarthy reunites with Aaron Rodgers, who finished as QB26 last season, so despite Michael Pittman and Rico Dowdle arriving, this projects as a low-ceiling, TD-scarce offense to underweight at 8.5 wins.

First-time play-caller Brian Fleury (Shanahan tree) keeps the Kubiak-style scheme on a 10.5-win roster, and with Zach Charbonnet's torn ACL, Jadarian Price steps into the lead-back lane while Rashid Shaheed's deep speed fits the non-PPR mold better than JSN's underneath volume.

Brock Purdy gets Mike Evans (age 33, coming off a career-low 12.1 PPG) and second-round pick De'Zhaun Stribling while Ricky Pearsall nurses PCL swelling and Christian Kirk a calf, and George Kittle is ahead of schedule on his Achilles for Week 1 (verify), but Christian McCaffrey's 450-touch 2025 is a blinking workload light.

New OC Zac Robinson brings McVay-style motion and pace for Baker Mayfield, who is playing without a new contract, with Emeka Egbuka (938 yards, 6 TDs as a rookie) the ascending non-PPR target over the aging Godwin and newcomer Kenneth Gainwell handling change-of-pace work.

New OC Brian Daboll says Cam Ward is picking up the offense very quickly, and with Wan'Dale Robinson locked in on $38M guaranteed and rookie Carnell Tate's pro-ready routes, Ward's mobility plus 6-pt passing TDs makes him a prime year-two QB target despite a 6.5 win total.

Dan Quinn promoted 31-year-old first-time play-caller David Blough, who plans to move Terry McLaurin all over the formation for a target spike, a plan that adds yardage upside but also unproven-play-caller risk to the whole Jayden Daniels stack.

breakout_watch.name: Omarion Hampton
breakout_watch.why: Mike McDaniel's Chargers scheme manufactures explosive runs and space touches for a back who already posted a 24.9-point week as a rookie; yardage-plus-TD profile is perfect for non-PPR.

breakout_watch.name: Ashton Jeanty
breakout_watch.why: Klint Kubiak is openly planning a Christian McCaffrey-style workload in a play-action run game; volume plus goal-line monopoly beats the bad-team concern at 10 yds/pt.

breakout_watch.name: Jeremiyah Love
breakout_watch.why: No. 3 overall pick with elite speed and a three-down skill set walking into an Arizona backfield he owns from day one; bad team, but untouched TD and yardage share.

breakout_watch.name: Bhayshul Tuten
breakout_watch.why: Scored 7 TDs on only 93 touches with a 31% missed-tackle-forced rate, and Travis Etienne's departure opens the Jacksonville backfield; TD efficiency is the whole game in this format.

breakout_watch.name: Jadarian Price
breakout_watch.why: Zach Charbonnet's torn ACL hands the explosive Notre Dame product (6.0 career YPC) the Seattle lead-back lane in a proven run scheme on a 10.5-win team.

breakout_watch.name: Jonathon Brooks
breakout_watch.why: Getting first-team reps over Chuba Hubbard and Canales says he looks like the pre-injury version; if the ACL history holds up he inherits a startable Carolina workload at a discount.

breakout_watch.name: Quinshon Judkins
breakout_watch.why: Fully healed fibula, 827 yards and 7 TDs as a rookie, and Cleveland's new run-first staff has no QB certainty, which funnels goal-line and early-down volume straight to him.

breakout_watch.name: Luther Burden III
breakout_watch.why: DJ Moore's exit vacates about 150 targets in Ben Johnson's top-6 offense and Burden's 2.92 YPRR is Nacua/JSN territory; downfield YAC yardage, not empty catches.

breakout_watch.name: Emeka Egbuka
breakout_watch.why: 938-yard, 6-TD rookie year and now a McVay-tree OC in Tampa raising pace and motion; ascending target share with real end-zone usage.

breakout_watch.name: Jayden Higgins
breakout_watch.why: Matched Nico Collins in TDs as a rookie on limited volume, and Houston's rebuilt OL should restore Stroud's downfield time; TD-per-target profile is a non-PPR cheat code.

breakout_watch.name: Cam Ward
breakout_watch.why: Brian Daboll built Josh Allen's breakout and says Ward is absorbing the offense quickly; rushing ability plus 6-pt passing TDs gives him a top-12 ceiling at a year-two price.

breakout_watch.name: Tyler Shough
breakout_watch.why: Closed his rookie season with six straight 17-plus-point games and New Orleans added Travis Etienne and rookie Jordyn Tyson around him; late-round 6-pt-TD value.

breakout_watch.name: Drake Maye
breakout_watch.why: Shoulder fully healed with no surgery, A.J. Brown imported as his alpha, and a 10.5 win total; his rushing floor plus new TD upside fits this scoring exactly.

breakout_watch.name: Kenneth Walker III
breakout_watch.why: Eric Bieniemy's Kansas City return comes with an explosive-run emphasis and Walker was signed to be that hammer; big-play yardage and scoring-position volume in a top offense.

fade_watch.name: Patrick Mahomes
fade_watch.why: Rehabbing a torn ACL and LCL and merely pushing for Week 1; even at 6-pt passing TDs, paying a healthy-Mahomes price for an availability question is the classic trap.

fade_watch.name: Christian McCaffrey
fade_watch.why: Coming off a 450-touch season at his age with his own injury history; the crash risk after that workload is exactly what non-PPR RB scarcity tempts you to ignore.

fade_watch.name: Josh Jacobs
fade_watch.why: 28 years old, 2,109 career touches, YPC down to 4.0; age-cliff plus efficiency decline means his TD total is propping up a fading yardage base.

fade_watch.name: James Conner
fade_watch.why: Buried on an Arizona depth chart behind No. 3 pick Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier with minimal first-team camp reps; name value far exceeds role.

fade_watch.name: Saquon Barkley
fade_watch.why: Yards before contact collapsed from 2.64 to 1.36 and Philadelphia is on another new play-caller installing a different run scheme; volume is safe, efficiency is not.

fade_watch.name: Matthew Stafford
fade_watch.why: Age-38 season after a QB2 finish; the market is paying for last year's outlier and any arm or back decline drags the whole Rams stack with him.

fade_watch.name: Mike Evans
fade_watch.why: Age 33, career-low 12.1 PPG last season, now learning a new offense in San Francisco behind an established target tree; the decade-long 1,000-yard autopilot is over.

fade_watch.name: Malik Nabers
fade_watch.why: ACL plus meniscus with a spring scar-tissue cleanup and no confirmed camp ramp-up; elite talent, but early-season availability and burst are genuinely unknown (verify).

fade_watch.name: Travis Hunter
fade_watch.why: Jacksonville plans to play him primarily at cornerback after his LCL tear, which guts the offensive snap share his WR draft price assumes.

fade_watch.name: Aaron Rodgers
fade_watch.why: Finished QB26 last year and the McCarthy reunion in Pittsburgh is nostalgia, not mechanism; low TD volume with none of the rushing that saves QBs in this format.

uncertainty_note: Most unsettled right now: the Atlanta QB room (Tua's back flare-up vs Penix's ACL clearance), whether Mahomes actually makes Week 1, the Bijan Robinson and Jahmyr Gibbs hold-ins, Malik Nabers' knee timeline, and Shemar Stewart's imaging results; several 2026 coaching-staff details (PHI and NYG head-coach structure, MIN QB pecking order, CLE/TB staff splits) come from secondary aggregation and carry (verify) tags where used.
